cases.text: PX4's battery-resistance estimate was 0 for the whole second half of the flight (it was already 0 when the vehicle took off), but BAT1_R_INTERNAL is set (5.0 mOhm per cell), so PX4 used that value, not the estimate.

PX4's battery-resistance estimate was 0 for the whole second half of the flight (it first reached 0 6.4 s after takeoff) while BAT1_R_INTERNAL is -1 (use the estimate), so PX4 did not correct the voltage-based state of charge for the voltage drop under load: it reads low under load and recovers after landing. On public PX4 flights this happened on 9 of 53 that use the estimate. A wrong current sensor scale or offset can also cause it. See PX4's battery estimation guide: https://docs.px4.io/main/en/config/battery
PX4's battery-resistance estimate did not collapse: it ended the flight at 10.5 mOhm per cell (public PX4 flights: median 2.7, p10-p90 1.2-7.5).
